card.name: "If" starting a conditional sentence after overdose statements
card.fires_on: The word "If" that opens a new sentence about what to do when an event occurs, mainly right after a statement that no data or no specific treatment exists for overdose. It also fires on "If" after a hypersensitivity warning.

modes.label: Overdose follow-up
modes.description: "If" starts the sentence right after "No data are available on overdose of [drug]" in the Overdosage section.
modes.example: 10 OVERDOSAGE No data are available on overdose of GENVOYA in patients.<< If>> overdose occurs, monitor the patient for evidence

modes.label: Allergic reaction follow-up
modes.description: "If" starts the sentence after a warning about previous hypersensitivity to penicillins.
modes.example: illin G, careful inquiry should be made concerning previous hypersensitivity reactions to penicillins, cephalosporins, or other allergens.<< If>> an allergic reaction occurs, penicillin

card.plain: It marks the "If" that begins a what-to-do-if-it-happens sentence, most often in the overdose section of a drug label.
